title: First on-device Agent flagship touched the safety red line upon launch? Douba AI denies involvement in game cheating

content_html:
Recently, the Nubia NaviX Ultra, equipped with ByteDance's "Doubao Mobile Assistant" under ZTE, encountered a prompt stating "abnormal device environment" and was forcibly kicked offline while running "Honor of Kings," triggering widespread attention on the conflict between AI edge-side system permissions and game anti-cheat mechanisms.

In response, Doubao Mobile Assistant issued an apology statement on its official community, emphasizing that the system did not interfere with Tencent games at any time. The AI did not engage in any violations such as illegal clicks, cheating, or simulated operations. It is currently continuing communication and coordination with Tencent and advising affected users to stop attempting to log in or submit account appeals through official channels.

As the world's first mass-produced AI agent flagship jointly developed by ZTE and ByteDance, the Nubia NaviX Ultra focuses on cross-app autonomous operations based on edge-side large models. The device began pre-orders on September 14, 2026, with pre-order numbers exceeding 370,000 on the single platform of JD.com the next day, and was officially released on September 16.

This incident highlights the boundary conflicts between edge-side AI system-level agents and existing security protection systems of mainstream applications when deeply interacting with the underlying system and scheduling across apps. As large model autonomous operation technology accelerates its penetration into terminal hardware, how to ensure AI cross-scenario execution efficiency while establishing trust mechanisms with third-party software has become a collaborative challenge that AI terminals must overcome to achieve large-scale commercialization.
